items.summary: Marina is the source of the report that the bridge was closed at night; the narrator/group has no other confirmations.

commitments.claim: Marina says that the bridge was closed at night.
commitments.scope: Reported attribution to Marina, not an unqualified narrator assertion.

preservation.object: Marina's attribution, the closure event, and its nighttime timing.
preservation.rationale: The reporting frame and its complement are overtly stated.

commitments.claim: The speaker's group has no confirmations other than Marina's report.

preservation.object: The absence of other confirmation, including the first-person plural perspective.
preservation.rationale: The second sentence explicitly limits the available confirmation.

unresolved: Who ‘we’ are, and whether the bridge was in fact closed, are not settled.

items.summary: Two cups stood on a table; an opposite armchair was still warm; Sergey said nothing.

commitments.claim: There were two cups on the table.

preservation.object: The number, cups, and their placement on the table.
preservation.rationale: This is directly asserted.

commitments.claim: The armchair opposite was still warm.

preservation.object: The chair's opposite relation and continued warmth.
preservation.rationale: Both are lexically expressed.

commitments.claim: Its warmth makes recent occupancy a defeasible inference, without identifying an occupant.

preservation.object: Availability of the ordinary recent-occupancy inference through the ‘still warm’ description.
preservation.rationale: A faithful rendering of continuing warmth should retain this natural inference, while not turning it into an assertion.

commitments.claim: Sergey said nothing.

preservation.object: Sergey's silence/non-speaking in the relevant situation.
preservation.rationale: It is directly stated.

unresolved: The reference point for ‘opposite’ and the identity of any recent occupant are unspecified.

items.summary: A wet umbrella lay at a stop, and nobody ever determined who left it.

commitments.claim: A wet umbrella was lying at the stop.

preservation.object: An umbrella, its wetness, and its location at a stop.
preservation.rationale: All three are stated.

commitments.claim: Nobody succeeded in finding out who left the umbrella.
commitments.scope: Narration about an unresolved investigation/knowledge state.

preservation.object: The failure to establish the person who left it, including the ‘eventually/still not’ aspect of так и.
preservation.rationale: The sentence explicitly reports that no one determined this.

unresolved: The owner, the person who left it, and why it is wet are not specified.

items.summary: The note contained exactly one quoted word, ‘no’.

commitments.claim: There was exactly one word on the note.

preservation.object: The exact one-word count.
preservation.rationale: Ровно explicitly marks exactness.

commitments.claim: That word was the quoted word ‘нет’.

preservation.object: The negative word's content and its presentation as the note's quoted written word.
preservation.rationale: The quotation and word identity are explicit; an idiomatic English equivalent is permitted by the shared policy.

unresolved: What the negative answers or who wrote the note are not given.

items.summary: A random passerby in the corridor uttered a declaration closing the meeting, but the chair continued the discussion.

commitments.claim: A random passerby from the corridor said, ‘I declare the meeting closed.’
commitments.scope: Narrated speech, attributed to an unidentified passerby.

preservation.object: The quoted declaration, its speaker as a random passerby, and the corridor setting.
preservation.rationale: The utterance and attribution are overt.

commitments.claim: The chair continued the discussion.

preservation.object: Continuation of the discussion by the chair.
preservation.rationale: This is explicitly asserted.

commitments.claim: The passerby's words are not established by the text as successfully closing the meeting.

preservation.object: The availability of the inference that the declaration lacked operative effect in this episode.
preservation.rationale: The passerby's description and the continued discussion jointly support this inference; it must not become an assertion of a general rule about authority.

unresolved: The passerby's authority, if any, and the formal status of the meeting are not independently specified.

items.summary: A translator says they have finally found a common language while taking a tongue prosthesis from a box, creating a deliberate idiomatic/literal juxtaposition.

commitments.claim: The translator said, ‘Well, at last we have found a common language.’
evidence: «Ну вот, наконец-то мы нашли общий язык»
commitments.scope: Quoted speech attributed to a translator.

preservation.object: The speaker, the finally/at-last aspect, and the quoted claim of achieving mutual linguistic understanding.
preservation.rationale: The quote and attribution are explicit.

commitments.claim: While speaking, the translator was taking a tongue prosthesis out of a box.

preservation.object: The action, box, and a prosthesis for a physical tongue.
preservation.rationale: The participial phrase expressly supplies these details.

commitments.claim: The shared Russian word язык links the idiomatic ‘common language’ phrase with the literal tongue prosthesis, producing incongruity/wordplay.
commitments.scope: A reading made available by the wording.

preservation.object: The availability of the idiomatic/literal lexical connection or a comparably intelligible wordplay effect.
preservation.rationale: The repeated polysemous word is deliberately foregrounded by the adjacent phrase and action; retaining only either reading loses this source-level relation.

unresolved: Whose prosthesis it is and whether it relates causally to the translator's linguistic success are not stated.
alternatives: The quotation can be read as the ordinary idiom for reaching mutual understanding, while the physical tongue reference activates a literal reading; both should remain accessible.

items.summary: Peter, specifically, refused to sign the contract; the others agreed.

commitments.claim: It was Peter in particular who refused to sign the contract.
commitments.scope: Narration with contrastive focus on Peter.

preservation.object: Peter's refusal, the signing of a contract, and the contrastive/exhaustive focus carried by именно.
preservation.rationale: Each is overtly encoded.

commitments.claim: The other relevant people agreed.
commitments.scope: Narration about the contextually relevant remainder, excluding Peter.

preservation.object: Agreement by the others relative to the relevant group.
preservation.rationale: The source explicitly contrasts them with Peter.

unresolved: The size and membership of the relevant group, and the precise object of the others' agreement, are contextually supplied rather than stated.

items.summary: Alice says the key is with Boris, while Boris says it is with Alice; the speaker/group does not know who is right.

commitments.claim: Alice says that the key is with Boris.

preservation.object: Alice's attribution and the content locating the key with Boris.
preservation.rationale: The source explicitly attributes this claim to Alice.

commitments.claim: Boris insists that the key is with Alice.
commitments.scope: Boris's assertion, with the force of уверяет.

preservation.object: Boris's attribution, its insistence/assurance force, and the opposing location claim.
preservation.rationale: The source expressly contrasts his statement with Alice's.

commitments.claim: The speaker/group does not know who is right.

preservation.object: The unresolved epistemic stance of ‘we’ toward the competing claims.
preservation.rationale: It is directly stated.

unresolved: The actual location of the key, whether either speaker is correct, and the identity of ‘we’ are not established.

items.summary: The speaker presents the train's having already left as an appearance or impression, not as certain fact.

commitments.claim: It seems that the train has already left.

preservation.object: The uncertainty/evidential qualification, the train's possible departure, and the ‘already’ relation to a reference time.
preservation.rationale: Кажется and уже are explicitly encoded; removing the former strengthens the claim.

unresolved: Whether the train actually left, the evidence for the appearance, and the relevant schedule/reference time are unspecified.

items.summary: The envelope contained nothing; Lena had concluded she was being pranked, then only in the evening noticed a letter stuck to the inside of a box lid.

commitments.claim: There was nothing in the envelope.
commitments.scope: Narration about the envelope's contents at the relevant time.

preservation.object: The envelope's absence of contents.
preservation.rationale: This is directly asserted.

commitments.claim: Lena had already decided that someone was playing a prank on her.

preservation.object: Lena's attributed conclusion, its prior/already timing, and its prank content without asserting the prank as fact.
preservation.rationale: The source attributes the conclusion to Lena.

commitments.claim: Only in the evening did Lena notice a letter glued to the inner side of the lid of a box.
evidence: приклеенное к внутренней стороне крышки коробки
commitments.scope: Narration about Lena's notice and the letter's physical location.

preservation.object: The late (‘only in the evening’) noticing, the letter, and its attachment to the inner side of a box lid.
preservation.rationale: These details and their order are explicitly stated.

commitments.claim: The ‘only in the evening’ wording supports that Lena had not noticed the letter earlier.

preservation.object: Availability of the delayed-discovery inference through an equivalent restrictive temporal expression.
preservation.rationale: Only restricts the time of her noticing; it does not assert that the letter was absent earlier.

unresolved: The relation between the envelope and the box, who attached the letter, and whether Lena really was pranked are not stated.
